newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N.'s Ekeus to visit Baghdad on Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: U.N.'s Ekeus to visit Baghdad on Feb 20.

text.p: Rolf Ekeus, chairman of the U.N. Commission (UNSCOM) disarming Iraq under the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire terms, will visit Baghdad on February 20 to try to defuse a stand-off over scrapped missile engines, a senior U.N. official said on Tuesday.

"The chairman is coming on the 20th of February...certainly the missile problem will be in the forefront," Goran Wallen director of Baghdad's Ongoing Monitoring and Verification Centre (OMV) told Reuters.

Wallen said Ekeus would also try to touch on remaining problems in the chemical arms whose destruction and that of the long-range missiles and biological weapons is a key condition for the removal of all curbs on oil exports by Iraq.

Iraq and UNSCOM have been at odds in the past few months over how and where to analyse more than 100 missile parts salvaged from sites close to Baghdad. About 80 of them are packed in boxes for shipment abroad and the rest are stored in warehouses under strict U.N. surveillance.

Iraq this month carried out large-scale excavation in search of evidence to try to prove to UNSCOM that it had no more banned missiles in its possession. Under Gulf War ceasefire terms, Iraq is forbidden from keeping or acquiring missiles with ranges greater than 150 km (93 miles).
